transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess what brings me in is... I’ve been waking up feeling really heavy and sad. Kind of hollow. Like I’m there, but there’s no spark in me anymore, even with dancing.
Did this start after a specific stressful event in your life?
Yeah… it was after I injured my ankle. That’s when this whole pattern started, and it’s been going on for about two months now.
Do you feel your sadness is mainly because of the ankle injury?

I think the ankle injury started it, but the sadness feels bigger than just being upset about my ankle. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like even when I think about dancing, there’s just no music in me.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I still care about the things I usually like, but lately it feels harder to feel anything from them. Like I go through the motions more than actually enjoying it.
Before this started, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had bad days like anyone, but I can’t really remember another stretch where it felt like this for days or weeks.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I don’t think I’ve had thoughts about hurting myself. I mean, I’ve felt really low and tired of feeling this way, but I haven’t been planning anything or wanting to do something to myself.
If your ankle had never been injured, do you think you would still be feeling this depressed?

I don’t know if it’s only the ankle. I think that made things harder, but what brought me in is this heavy, hollow sadness I keep waking up with. It feels like… even if I imagine being back in the studio, the music just isn’t in me the same way.
Since this started, have you been waking up earlier than usual and unable to get back to sleep?

Yes. Lately I’ll fall asleep because I’m exhausted, but then I wake up around four or five in the morning and can’t really get back to sleep. My stomach feels tight when I wake up. Before that, some nights I was barely sleeping at all, staying up sketching formations until almost dawn.
Since this started, have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot of the time?
I’m not sure. I’ve been tense sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m on edge all the time. It’s more like I feel worn down than anxious.
Since this started, has your appetite changed?

Yeah, it has. When I was kind of buzzing with ideas, I’d forget to eat or just skip meals without noticing. Now I’ll try to eat and it just tastes like cardboard. My rehearsal clothes have been fitting looser lately.
During the time you were barely sleeping and felt like you were buzzing with ideas, did you also feel unusually energized or high?

Yes. There were times I felt really alive, like everything was clear and possible. Almost dazzling, I guess. But I’d also get angry fast if someone questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down because of my ankle.
During those times you felt dazzling and full of ideas, did you feel more confident or powerful than usual?

Yes. I really did. I felt like I could turn the whole setback into something huge — like a career-defining piece that would change how people think about dance and wilderness. And honestly, I was surprised people didn’t just immediately see what I saw.
During that time when you felt dazzling and slept very little, were you doing much more than usual toward your projects or other activities?

Yes. Even with my injury, I was constantly doing something. I’d go from drawing maps to emailing collaborators to reorganizing music files, and then I’d try to redesign the whole project all at once. It felt like I couldn’t really stop or slow down.
During that time when you felt dazzling and needed very little sleep, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think there was anything clearly risky like that, at least nothing that stands out to me. I was intense and impulsive with the project, but I can’t think of a specific dangerous thing I did.
During that time when you felt dazzling and needed very little sleep, did you ever hear or see things that other people couldn’t?

Yes. A few times, on the really wired days, I heard this low humming voice… almost like wind moving over rock. It seemed like it was telling me where the dancers should go, even though I was alone in my apartment and the windows were closed.
Have you heard that humming voice during this current sad, heavy period?

No, not during this current sad period. The humming voice and those “messages” from the mountains only happened when I was really wired and barely sleeping, racing through all those plans. Since I’ve been feeling low, I still feel guilty and slowed down, but I haven’t heard the voice or felt like signs were directing me.
